definition_zh: 手推车；购物车；马车；用车运送
definition_en: a small vehicle with wheels that is pushed by hand or pulled by an animal, used for carrying goods
core_image: 轮子上架一块平板：靠人力或牲口拖着走
scene: 超市的过道里，她一边看货架一边往前走。She pushed the cart past the shelves and dropped a loaf of bread into it.
sceneCN: 这里 cart 指「购物车」（第 1 个义项：超市里用手推的载物车）；句意是她推着购物车经过货架，把一条面包放了进去。

senses.title: A small vehicle pushed by hand
senses.definition: a small wheeled vehicle that a person pushes, used for carrying goods in shops or on streets
senses.definitionCN: 一种带轮的小型载物车，由人推着走，用于在商店或街道上运送东西
senses.example: She pushed the cart to the checkout counter.
senses.exampleCN: 她把购物车推到收银台。
senses.why: The core image is a flat board on wheels, and a hand-pushed trolley is that image in its simplest modern form.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是架在轮子上的平板，而人手推的购物车正是这一意象最简单的现代形态。

senses.title: A wagon pulled by an animal
senses.definition: a two-wheeled or four-wheeled vehicle pulled by a horse or other animal, used in farming and transport
senses.definitionCN: 由马或其他牲口拉动的两轮或四轮大车，用于农活和运输
senses.example: The farmer loaded the hay onto a wooden cart.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫把干草装上一辆木制大车。
senses.why: Once the wheeled board is large enough to need a beast of burden, the same word covers the farm wagon.
senses.whyCN: 当带轮的平板大到需要牲口来拉动时，同一个词自然就覆盖了农用大车。

senses.title: To carry something with effort
senses.definition: to carry or move something in a cart, or to carry something heavy with obvious effort
senses.definitionCN: 用车子运送某物，或很费力地搬运重物
senses.example: They carted the old furniture up three flights of stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把那件旧家具费力地搬上三层楼。
senses.why: If a cart is the tool for moving loads, the verb names the whole act of hauling those loads.
senses.whyCN: 既然大车就是搬重物的工具，动词便顺势指代了整个搬运动作。

intro.en: Cart is a Germanic word that reached English from Old Norse rather than from Latin, which is why it has no Latin relatives in this entry.
intro.cn: cart 是日耳曼语词，经由古诺斯语进入英语，而不是来自拉丁语，所以本条没有拉丁同族词。

items.en: A reconstructed noun for a wheeled carrier, generally connected with the base that also produced car.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个表示带轮载具的原始日耳曼语名词，与产生 car 的词根相关。

items.en: Old Norse kartr named a small two-wheeled wagon and came south with Norse settlement in England.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 kartr 指一种两轮小车，随北欧移民进入英格兰。

items.en: Cart is recorded in the thirteenth century as the everyday word for a farm or market wagon.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，cart 在十三世纪已有记录，是农用和集市运货车的日常说法。

items.en: The word spreads to any low wheeled platform, including hand carts used in towns.
items.cn: 此后该词扩展到任何低矮的带轮平台，包括城镇里使用的手推车。

items.en: Modern English adds the shopping cart, the golf cart and the verb sense of hauling something with effort.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上购物车、高尔夫球车，以及费力搬运的动词义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Germanic stem, while the meaning group gathers other wheeled carriers.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同一日耳曼词干构成的词，近义组收的是其他带轮载具。

entries.definition: a person who drives or works with a cart
entries.definitionCN: 赶车人；以赶车为业的人

entries.definition: the work or charge of moving goods by cart
entries.definitionCN: 用车运输的工作或运费

entries.definition: as much as a cart can carry
a large four-wheeled vehicle for carrying heavy loads
entries.definitionCN: 运载重物的大型四轮车

entries.definition: a small wheeled frame or basket pushed by hand
entries.definitionCN: 用手推的带轮小车或篮子

entries.definition: a small hand cart with one wheel at the front
entries.definitionCN: 前部只有一个轮子的手推小车

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the link with car, the common compounds and the verb pattern of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子利用它与 car 的联系、常见复合词以及动词用法。

normal.en: Cart differs from car by one letter, and a cart is in effect a car stripped of its engine.
normal.cn: cart 比 car 只多一个字母，而大车实际上就是卸掉发动机的汽车。

normal.en: The fixed phrase shopping cart ties the word to the supermarket aisle.
normal.cn: 固定搭配 shopping cart 把这个词牢牢拴在超市过道上。

normal.en: The suffix -er in carter marks the person, exactly as in driver and worker.
normal.cn: carter 里的后缀 -er 表示人，与 driver、worker 的构词方式一样。

normal.en: Cart away and cart off both suggest taking something away in a loaded cart.
normal.cn: cart away 与 cart off 都表示用装满货的车把东西拉走。

normal.en: The plural carts and the third-person carts look identical, so only the sentence tells you which is which.
normal.cn: 复数 carts 与三单 carts 拼写相同，只能靠句子判断是名词还是动词。

abstract.en: Picture a squeaking wheel rolling down a supermarket aisle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只吱吱作响的轮子在超市过道里滚动。

abstract.en: Picture a horse straining against the shafts of a wooden cart.
abstract.cn: 想象一匹马绷紧车辕，拉着一辆木车。

abstract.en: Picture yourself heaving a load of bricks onto a low platform with wheels.
abstract.cn: 想象自己把一摞砖费力地抬上带轮的低矮平板。

examples.en: He loaded the boxes onto the cart.
examples.cn: 他把箱子装上了手推车。

examples.en: The farmer carted the hay to the barn.
examples.cn: 农夫把干草运到了谷仓。

examples.en: A cart blocked the narrow street.
examples.cn: 一辆大车堵住了狭窄的街道。

dict_mnemonic.text: cart 比 car 多一个 t：像一辆卸掉发动机的小汽车，只剩下带轮子的载货平板。

root: 古诺斯语 kartr（双轮车）借入中古英语，与 car 同出一支日耳曼语词，本义是带轮的载物工具。

sensesIntro.en: One core shape, a board on wheels, gives a hand trolley, an animal wagon and finally the act of hauling loads.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个核心形状，即架在轮子上的平板，先后长出手推车、牲口大车，最后长出搬运这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat board on wheels, moved by hand or by an animal.
core.cn: 核心意象：架在轮子上的平板，靠人力或牲口拖动。

branches.en: The hand-pushed trolley keeps the small size and the human power.
branches.cn: 手推车保留了小巧的尺寸和人力推动的方式。

branches.en: The wagon scales the same platform up until an animal supplies the pull.
branches.cn: 大车把同一块平板放大，直到改由牲口提供拉力。

branches.en: The verb turns the tool into the action of moving a load.
branches.cn: 动词义把工具转成了搬运货物的动作。

branches.en: Both nouns share wheels, a flat load bed and short-distance work.
branches.cn: 两个名词义都共享轮子、平载货面和短途作业这三个特征。

branches.en: Heavy hauling links the farm wagon with the effortful verb sense.
branches.cn: 沉重的拖运把农用大车与费力的动词义连在一起。

intro.en: Cart builds almost nothing with classical affixes; its family grows through inflection and compounding.
intro.cn: cart 几乎不用古典词缀构词，它的词族靠屈折变化和复合构词扩展。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin and has no Latin ancestor, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 该词源自日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: The cart is by the door.

items.example: Two carts stood in the yard.
Carting stones all day is hard work.

items.meaning: a person who drives a cart
items.example: The carter waited at the market.
Cartage was added to the bill.
They bought a cartload of apples.

items.meaning: the wheel of a cart, or a sideways roll
items.example: The child turned a cartwheel on the grass.
items.exampleCN: 孩子在草地上翻了个侧手翻。

definition_zh: 动画片；漫画；讽刺画；草图
definition_en: a film made from a series of drawings, or a drawing that tells a joke or a story
core_image: 先画在硬纸板上的草图，后来一帧帧动了起来
scene: 孩子放学回家，丢下书包就打开电视。He laughed at the cartoon playing on Saturday morning.
sceneCN: 这里 cartoon 指「动画片」（第 1 个义项：由连续图画拍成的影片）；句意是他看着周六早上播放的动画片笑了。

senses.title: An animated film
senses.definition: a film made by photographing a series of drawings so that they appear to move
senses.definitionCN: 把一连串图画拍摄下来、使其看起来会动的影片
senses.example: The children watch a cartoon every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们每天早上都看动画片。
senses.why: The core image of drawings on strong paper turns into motion once those drawings are filmed in sequence.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是画在厚纸上的图画，当这些图画被连续拍摄，它就动了起来。

senses.title: A humorous drawing
senses.definition: a drawing in a newspaper or magazine that makes a joke or comments on events
senses.definitionCN: 报纸或杂志上带有玩笑或评论意味的图画
senses.example: The paper printed a cartoon about the election.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸刊登了一幅关于选举的漫画。
senses.why: A single strong drawing keeps the paper sketch but adds a caption and a target to laugh at.
senses.whyCN: 单幅有力的图画保留了纸面草图，又加上文字说明和嘲讽对象。

senses.title: A preparatory sketch
senses.definition: a full-size drawing made as a preparation for a painting or tapestry
senses.definitionCN: 为绘画或挂毯所作的等大预备图稿
senses.example: The museum keeps the cartoon for the ceiling fresco.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆保存着那幅天顶壁画的底稿。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the sketch was literally drawn on cartone, a sheet of strong paper.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：草图字面上就画在 cartone，也就是一张厚纸板上。

intro.en: Cartoon travels from Latin paper to Italian cardboard to a French drawing sheet, and only later picks up its comic and animated senses.
intro.cn: cartoon 从拉丁语的纸，到意大利语的厚纸板，再到法语的大幅画纸，很晚才获得漫画与动画的含义。

items.en: Charta meant papyrus or paper and underlies many European words for paper and card.
items.cn: 拉丁语 charta 指纸草或纸张，是许多欧洲语言中纸与卡片类词的源头。

items.en: Cartone, an augmentative of carta, named a large sheet of strong paper or cardboard.
items.cn: 意大利语 cartone 由 carta 加大后缀构成，指一大张厚纸或纸板。

items.en: French carton carried the word into the language of art workshops as a full-size drawing on paper.
items.cn: 法语 carton 把该词带进画坊用语，指画在纸上的等大图稿。

items.en: English borrowed cartoon for a preparatory drawing, especially one for a fresco or tapestry.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 cartoon，指壁画或挂毯的预备图稿。

items.en: Punch magazine applied the word to humorous drawings, and the comic sense took over.
items.cn: 十九世纪《笨拙》杂志用它指幽默图画，漫画义由此流行。

items.en: Filmed drawings added the animated sense in the twentieth century, now the most familiar one.
items.cn: 二十世纪活动的图画电影又添上动画片义，如今这是最熟悉的用法。

note.en: The first group follows the paper-and-card root, the second gathers other kinds of comic or animated pictures.
note.cn: 第一组沿纸与纸板的词根展开，第二组收其他漫画与动画类图画。

entries.definition: a container made of cardboard
an artist who draws cartoons
exaggerated in the style of a cartoon
the technique of making drawings or models appear to move
entries.definitionCN: 让图画或模型看起来会动的技术

entries.definition: a magazine or strip of drawings telling a funny story
entries.definitionCN: 讲述滑稽故事的漫画刊物或连环画

entries.definition: a drawing that exaggerates a person's features for comic effect
entries.definitionCN: 夸张人物特征以取得滑稽效果的画像

normalIntro.en: These hooks rest on the cardboard root, the fixed compounds and the artist suffixes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子依托纸板这一词根、固定复合词以及表示画者的后缀。

normal.en: Cartoon and carton share a root: a cartoon began as a drawing on strong cardboard.
normal.cn: cartoon 与 carton 同根：漫画最初就画在厚纸板上。

normal.en: The suffix -ist makes cartoonist, a person, just as it does in artist and pianist.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ist 构成 cartoonist，表示人，和 artist、pianist 一样。

normal.en: Animated cartoon spells out the moving-picture sense inside the phrase.
normal.cn: animated cartoon 这一搭配直接把会动的影片义写了出来。

normal.en: Political cartoon fixes the newspaper sense with a clear target.
normal.cn: political cartoon 用明确的嘲讽对象固定了报纸漫画义。

normal.en: The ending -oon also appears in balloon and lagoon, all words borrowed from French or Italian.
normal.cn: 词尾 -oon 也出现在 balloon 和 lagoon 里，这些词都借自法语或意大利语。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of drawings flipped quickly until the figures run.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠画稿被快速翻动，画中人竟然跑了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a small boxed drawing in the corner of a newspaper.
abstract.cn: 想象报纸角落里一幅加了框的小画。

abstract.en: Picture a painter sketching a huge design on thick grey paper.
abstract.cn: 想象画师在厚厚的灰纸上勾出巨大的图样。

examples.en: My sister draws a cartoon for the school paper.
examples.cn: 我妹妹为校报画漫画。

examples.en: The cartoon made fun of the mayor.
examples.cn: 那幅漫画拿市长开玩笑。

examples.en: He watched cartoons all afternoon.
examples.cn: 他整个下午都在看动画片。

dict_mnemonic.text: cartoon 开头像 cart（车）：把它想成一辆装满画稿的小车，一开动就变成了动画。

root: 意大利语 cartone（厚纸板）经法语进入英语，本义是画在厚纸上的大幅草图，后指漫画与动画片。

sensesIntro.en: The paper sketch gives a preparatory drawing, a newspaper joke and finally a filmed sequence of drawings.
sensesIntro.cn: 纸上的草图先长成预备图稿，再长成报纸上的笑话，最后长成连续拍摄的动画。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawing made on a sheet of strong paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：画在一张厚纸上的图画。

branches.en: The earliest sense keeps the drawing and the paper untouched.
branches.cn: 最早的义项原样保留了图画与纸张。

branches.en: A caption and a target turn the sketch into a joke.
branches.cn: 加上说明文字与嘲讽对象，草图就变成了笑话。

branches.en: Filming many drawings in order adds motion to the same image.
branches.cn: 把许多图画按顺序拍摄，就给同一画面加上了运动。

branches.en: Both senses stay on paper, one as preparation and one as comment.
branches.cn: 这两个义项都留在纸面上，一个用于准备，一个用于评论。

branches.en: Both are popular visual stories, one static and one moving.
branches.cn: 两者都是通俗的视觉故事，一个静止，一个会动。

intro.en: Cartoon forms a small family through inflection, the artist suffix and two adjective endings.
intro.cn: cartoon 通过屈折变化、表人后缀和两个形容词词尾形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The deeper source is Latin charta, paper, which also gives chart and charter.
latinIntro.cn: 更深的源头是拉丁语 charta（纸），chart 与 charter 也出自这里。

items.exampleCN: 那个反派笑得十分夸张。

definition_zh: 情况；实例；案件；病例；箱子
definition_en: a particular situation, an instance of something, a matter decided in court, or a container that holds something
core_image: 一个把内容罩住的框：事情落进来，东西装进去
scene: 会议上大家都在讨论同一个问题。In this case, the manager agreed to wait another week.
sceneCN: 这里 case 指「情况」（第 1 个义项：某种具体情形）；句意是在这种情况下，经理同意再等一周。

pos.zh: 情况；实例；案件；病例；箱子

senses.title: A particular situation
senses.definition: a particular situation or set of circumstances that exists at a certain time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻存在的特定情形或一组状况
senses.example: In that case, we should leave early.
senses.exampleCN: 既然那样，我们该早点走。
senses.why: The Latin source meant something that falls out, and a situation is exactly what has fallen into place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源义是「落下来的事」，而情况正是落到眼前、摆在那里的事。

senses.title: An example or instance
senses.definition: a single example of something happening, especially in an argument or report
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的一个单独例子，尤用于论证或报告
senses.example: The report lists several cases of fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了好几起欺诈实例。
senses.why: One fallen event can stand as a sample for a whole class of events.
senses.whyCN: 一件落下来的事可以充当一整类事件的样本。

senses.title: A matter for a court
senses.definition: a question or dispute that is brought before a court of law
senses.definitionCN: 提交到法庭审理的问题或纠纷
senses.example: The lawyer took the case without a fee.
senses.exampleCN: 律师免费接了这桩案子。
senses.why: A legal case is simply one situation singled out and placed before a judge.
senses.whyCN: 法律案件无非是被单独挑出来、送到法官面前的一种情形。

senses.title: A patient or an illness
senses.definition: a person suffering from an illness, or an occurrence of a disease recorded by a doctor
senses.definitionCN: 患某种病的人，或医生记录的一次发病
senses.example: The clinic reported three new cases of flu.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所报告了三例新的流感病例。
senses.why: Medicine counts each separate instance of illness, so the instance sense is applied to patients.
senses.whyCN: 医学把每一次发病都单独计数，于是「实例」义就用到了病人身上。

senses.title: A container that holds something
senses.definition: a container designed to hold and protect a particular object
senses.definitionCN: 为装放并保护某物而设计的容器
senses.example: He put the violin back in its case.
senses.exampleCN: 他把小提琴放回琴盒。
senses.why: This sense has a different source, Latin capsa, a box, and only later merged in spelling with the situation word.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项另有来源，拉丁语 capsa 就是盒子，后来才在拼写上并入表示情况的词。

intro.en: Case in English is two words in one shape: an event word from Latin casus and a container word from Latin capsa.
intro.cn: 英语里的 case 是两种词形合一：表示事件的词来自拉丁语 casus，表示容器的词来自拉丁语 capsa。

items.en: Casus meant a fall or something that befalls, from cadere, to fall.
items.cn: 拉丁语 casus 意为落下或落到头上的事，源自动词 cadere（落下）。

items.en: Capsa meant a box or case, and also gives English capsule and cash.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capsa 意为盒子或箱子，也是英语 capsule 与 cash 的来源。

items.en: Old French cas carried the event sense into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 诺曼征服之后，古法语 cas 把事件义带进了英语。

items.en: Middle English case covers both a happening and a box, the two strands now spelled alike.
items.cn: 中古英语的 case 同时指发生的事和盒子，两条线此时拼写已经相同。

items.en: Legal and medical usage fixes the court case and the patient case as standard phrases.
items.cn: 十六至十八世纪，法律与医学用法把法庭案件和病例固定为常见说法。

items.en: Modern grammars and manuals add case study, casework and other compound labels.
items.cn: 现代语法书和手册又添上个案研究、个案工作等复合说法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the container branch, while the meaning group gathers words for situations and disputes.
note.cn: 形近组沿容器这一支展开，近义组收表示情形与纠纷的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the fixed phrase in case, the falling root and the separate box root.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用固定搭配 in case、表示落下的词根，以及另一个表示盒子的词根。

normal.en: In case is a set phrase meaning just in case something happens, not a case in a court.
normal.cn: in case 是固定说法，意为以防万一，与法庭案件无关。

normal.en: The event sense comes from cadere, to fall, so a case is something that falls into your path.
normal.cn: 事件义来自 cadere（落下），所以 case 就是落到你眼前的事。

normal.en: The box sense comes from capsa, which also gives capsule, a small case for medicine.
normal.cn: 箱子义来自 capsa，capsule（胶囊）也是这个词源。

normal.en: Case study, court case and pencil case each fix one sense in a familiar phrase.
normal.cn: case study、court case、pencil case 各自把一个义项固定在熟悉的搭配里。

normal.en: Only the plural cases is needed for the noun, so the form list stays short.
normal.cn: 名词只需要复数 cases，所以形式表很短。

abstract.en: Picture a folder dropped on a desk with all the facts inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件夹落在桌上，里面装满了事实。

abstract.en: Picture a violin lying in a velvet-lined box.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小提琴躺在铺着绒布的盒子里。

abstract.en: Picture a judge holding up one thin file among many.
abstract.cn: 想象法官从许多档案中举起薄薄的一份。

examples.en: In most cases the train arrives on time.
examples.cn: 大多数情况下火车都准点到达。

examples.en: The police are still working on the case.
examples.cn: 警方仍在处理这起案件。

examples.en: Put your glasses back in the case.
examples.cn: 把眼镜放回眼镜盒里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 case 想成一个带锁的盒子：里面装着情况、案件和病例这些内容。

root: 情况义源自拉丁语 casus（落下、发生的事），箱子义源自拉丁语 capsa（盒），两个词在英语中同形合并。

sensesIntro.en: From one fallen event grow the instance, the situation, the court case and the medical case, while a separate box root adds the container.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一件落下的事长出实例、情况、案件和病例，另一支表示盒子的词根则添上容器义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frame that holds what falls into it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个把落进来的东西框住的外壳。

branches.en: A situation is the whole set of things that have fallen into place.
branches.cn: 情况就是已经落到位置上的一整套事情。

branches.en: An instance is one such event picked out and counted.
branches.cn: 实例就是从其中挑出并计数的一件。

branches.en: A court case is the same event handed to a judge.
branches.cn: 案件就是把同一件事交给法官处理。

branches.en: A medical case applies the counting sense to sick patients.
branches.cn: 病例把计数的用法用到了病人身上。

branches.en: The container sense comes from a different root that happens to look the same.
branches.cn: 容器义来自另一个恰好同形的词根。

intro.en: Case expands mainly by compounding and by the -ing and -ment endings, not by classical prefixes.
intro.cn: case 主要靠复合构词以及 -ing、-ment 词尾扩展，不靠古典前缀。

latinIntro.en: Two Latin nouns stand behind the English word: casus for events and capsa for boxes.
latinIntro.cn: 英语这个词背后有两个拉丁名词：表示事件的 casus 和表示盒子的 capsa。

items.example: Casework takes most of her day.
items.exampleCN: 个案工作占了她大半天。

items.meaning: a display case or a chance to show off
items.example: The hall was a showcase for new art.
items.exampleCN: 大厅成了新艺术的展示场。

items.example: He left his briefcase on the train.
items.exampleCN: 他把公文包落在火车上了。

items.meaning: a piece of furniture with shelves
items.example: A tall bookcase filled the wall.

latinEntries.example: Casus is the source of the event sense.
latinEntries.exampleCN: casus 是事件义的来源。

latinEntries.example: Capsa also gives capsule and cash.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capsa 也是 capsule 与 cash 的来源。

definition_zh: 现金；现款；兑现；赚钱
definition_en: money in the form of coins and notes, or to exchange a cheque for money
core_image: 钱箱里随时能拿出来的现钱
scene: 结账时收银员问怎么付款。She paid in cash and put the receipt in her bag.
sceneCN: 这里 cash 指「现金」（第 1 个义项：硬币和纸币形式的钱）；句意是她付了现金，把收据放进包里。

senses.title: Money in coins and notes
senses.definition: money in the form of coins and banknotes rather than cheques or cards
senses.definitionCN: 以硬币和纸币形式存在的钱，而非支票或银行卡
senses.example: He always carries some cash for the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 他总带些现金坐公交。
senses.why: The Latin source meant a money box, and the word shifted from the box to the ready money kept inside it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源义是钱箱，词义从箱子转到箱子里随时可取的现钱。

senses.title: To exchange a cheque for money
senses.definition: to give or receive coins and notes in exchange for a cheque or other paper
senses.definitionCN: 用支票或其他票据换取硬币和纸币
senses.example: She cashed her salary cheque at the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 她在银行把工资支票兑成了现金。
senses.why: If cash is ready money, the verb names the act of turning paper into that ready money.
senses.whyCN: 既然 cash 是现钱，动词就指把票据变成现钱的动作。

senses.title: Funds available to a business
senses.definition: money that a company or person has available to spend at once
senses.definitionCN: 公司或个人当下可以动用的钱
senses.example: The firm ran out of cash in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在春天耗尽了资金。
senses.why: For a business, ready money on hand becomes a measure of health, so cash stands for available funds.
senses.whyCN: 对企业而言，手头的现钱成了经营健康的尺度，于是 cash 代指可动用资金。

intro.en: Cash goes back to a Latin word for a box, then to the money box and finally to the money inside.
intro.cn: cash 可追到拉丁语表示盒子的词，再经钱箱义，最后指箱子里的钱。

items.en: Capsa was a box or case, the container that held valuables.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capsa 指盒子或箱子，用来盛放贵重物品。

items.en: Italian cassa named a chest or money box in banking and trade.
items.cn: 意大利语 cassa 在金融和贸易中指钱柜或钱箱。

items.en: Middle French casse carried the money-box sense into northern Europe.
items.cn: 中古法语 casse 把钱箱义带到了北欧。

items.en: English cash first names a money box and soon the coin kept in it.
items.cn: 英语 cash 先指钱箱，很快又指箱里存放的硬币。

items.en: Banking adds the verb sense of cashing a cheque and the phrase cash flow.
items.cn: 银行业务又添上兑现支票的动词义和现金流这一说法。

note.en: The first group shares the money-box root, the second lists other words for money and payment.
note.cn: 第一组共享钱箱这一词根，第二组列出其他表示钱与支付的词。

entries.definition: a person who takes and pays out money
working without coins or notes
a record of money received and paid
the money used in a country
a piece of metal money
an amount paid or the act of paying
entries.definitionCN: 支付的款项或付款行为

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the money-box root, the fixed banking phrases and the short verb forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用钱箱词根、固定银行搭配，以及简短的动词形式。

normal.en: Cash and case share a Latin root meaning box, so cash is literally the money in the box.
normal.cn: cash 与 case 共享表示盒子的拉丁词根，cash 字面上就是箱子里的钱。

normal.en: A cashier is the person at the box, the one who takes and gives money.
normal.cn: cashier 就是守着钱箱的人，负责收钱和付钱。

normal.en: Cash flow pictures money moving in and out like water through a pipe.
normal.cn: cash flow 把钱的进出想象成水流过管道。

normal.en: Pay in cash is the everyday phrase that keeps the noun sense alive.
normal.cn: pay in cash 是让名词义保持活跃的日常说法。

normal.en: The third person cashes and the past cashed both keep the short -sh stem.
normal.cn: 三单 cashes 和过去式 cashed 都保留了短短的 -sh 词干。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden box overflowing with coins on a shop counter.
abstract.cn: 想象商店柜台上一个装满硬币的木箱。

abstract.en: Picture notes folded into a wallet before a trip.
abstract.cn: 想象出门前把纸币折好塞进钱包。

abstract.en: Picture a cheque turning into a stack of notes at the bank window.
abstract.cn: 想象一张支票在银行窗口变成一叠钞票。

examples.en: I have no cash with me today.
examples.cn: 我今天身上没带现金。

examples.en: Can you cash this cheque for me?
examples.cn: 你能帮我兑现这张支票吗？

examples.en: The shop only accepts cash.
examples.cn: 这家店只收现金。

dict_mnemonic.text: cash 读音接近「喀什」：想象在喀什的集市上掏出现金买东西。

root: 源自拉丁语 capsa（盒），经意大利语 cassa、中古法语 casse 进入英语，本指钱箱，后指箱中的现钱。

sensesIntro.en: A money box gives the ready money inside it, then the act of turning paper into that money, then the funds a business holds.
sensesIntro.cn: 钱箱先给出箱里的现钱，再给出把票据换成现钱的动作，最后给出企业持有的资金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a box of ready money kept close at hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着现钱、随手可取的钱箱。

branches.en: The notes and coins in the box become the everyday cash sense.
branches.cn: 箱里的纸币和硬币成了日常的现金义。

branches.en: The verb turns a cheque into the contents of the box.
branches.cn: 动词义把支票变成箱子里的东西。

branches.en: For a company the box stands for the funds it can spend now.
branches.cn: 对公司来说，这只箱子代表它眼下能动用的资金。

branches.en: Both senses turn on the same contrast between paper claims and real money.
branches.cn: 两个义项都围绕票据与真钱之间的同一对照。

branches.en: Ready money is both what you carry and what a business measures.
branches.cn: 现钱既是随身携带的钱，也是企业衡量的指标。

intro.en: Cash grows a compact family through the -ier and -less endings and a few compounds.
intro.cn: cash 通过 -ier、-less 词尾和少量复合词形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The ultimate source is Latin capsa, a box, which also underlies case and capsule.
latinIntro.cn: 最终源头是拉丁语 capsa（盒子），case 与 capsule 也出自这里。

items.example: Cash is king in small shops.

items.meaning: he or she exchanges for money
items.example: She cashes her cheque on Fridays.
He cashed the cheque at noon.
Cashing a cheque takes a minute.
The cashier counted the notes twice.
items.exampleCN: 收银员把钞票数了两遍。

items.example: The city is almost cashless now.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市如今几乎不用现金。

items.meaning: a book recording money paid and received
items.example: Every entry goes into the cashbook.

items.meaning: the movement of money in and out
items.exampleCN: 出售之后现金流好转了。

latinEntries.example: Capsa is the deep source of cash.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capsa 是 cash 的深层来源。

latinEntries.example: Cassa named the chest in old banks.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cassa 在老式银行里指钱柜。

definition_zh: 收银员；出纳员；革职；罢免
definition_en: a person who receives and pays out money in a shop or bank, or to dismiss someone from a position of service
core_image: 守在钱箱旁清点钱款的人
scene: 超市收银台前排着长队。The cashier scanned each item and told her the total.
sceneCN: 这里 cashier 指「收银员」（第 1 个义项：在商店收款的人）；句意是收银员逐件扫码，告诉她总价。

senses.title: A person who handles payments
senses.definition: a person whose job is to take money from customers or to pay money out at a bank
senses.definitionCN: 负责向顾客收款或在银行付钱的工作人员
senses.example: The cashier gave me the wrong change.
senses.exampleCN: 收银员找错了钱。
senses.why: The French source meant the keeper of the money box, so the person is named after the box itself.
senses.whyCN: 法语源词指看管钱箱的人，所以这个人是按那只钱箱来命名的。

senses.title: To dismiss from service
senses.definition: to dismiss an officer or official from a position, usually with disgrace
senses.definitionCN: 把军官或官员免职，通常带有不光彩的意味
senses.example: The colonel was cashiered for neglect of duty.
senses.exampleCN: 那名上校因玩忽职守被革职。
senses.why: This verb comes from a different source meaning to break or discard, and it pictures the box of office being thrown away.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词另有来源，意为打破或丢弃，画面是把职权这只盒子扔掉。

intro.en: The shop sense comes from a French word for the keeper of a money box, while the dismissal sense comes from a separate verb meaning to break or discard.
intro.cn: 商店义来自法语中看管钱箱的人，革职义则来自另一个意为打破或丢弃的动词。

items.en: Capsa, a box, underlies the French words for a money chest and its keeper.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capsa（盒子）是法语中钱柜及其看管者说法的源头。

items.en: Caisse named a money box and caissier the person who kept it.
items.cn: 法语 caisse 指钱箱，caissier 指看管它的人。

items.en: English borrowed cashier for the officer who handled a company's money.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 cashier，指管理公司钱款的职员。

items.en: A separate verb, recorded as casseren or casser, meant to break and then to dismiss.
items.cn: 另有一个动词，记作 casseren 或 casser，本义为打破，后指免职。

items.en: Modern English keeps both strands: the shop worker and the disgraced officer.
items.cn: 现代英语两条线都保留：商店职员与被革职的军官。

note.en: The first group follows the money-box root, the second gathers people who handle money at a counter.
note.cn: 第一组沿钱箱词根展开，第二组收在柜台处理钱款的人。

entries.definition: coins and notes used as money
entries.definitionCN: 作为货币的硬币和纸币

entries.definition: the act of dismissing an officer
a book recording money received and paid
a bank clerk who pays out money
a person who keeps records or serves customers
entries.definitionCN: 管账或接待顾客的职员

entries.definition: the person in charge of a group's money

normalIntro.en: These hooks link cashier to cash, to the -ier ending and to the separate dismissal verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 cashier 与 cash、-ier 词尾以及另一个革职动词联系起来。

normal.en: Cashier is cash plus -ier, the person who deals with the cash all day.
normal.cn: cashier 就是 cash 加 -ier，整天与现金打交道的人。

normal.en: The ending -ier also marks a person in soldier and courier.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ier 在 soldier 和 courier 里同样表示人。

normal.en: Bank cashier and head cashier fix the job sense in two short phrases.
normal.cn: bank cashier 与 head cashier 用两个短搭配固定了职业义。

normal.en: Cashiered is almost always used of officers, which keeps the dismissal sense apart.
normal.cn: cashiered 几乎只用于军官，这使革职义与收银义区分开来。

normal.en: The spelling keeps one s and a double s sound, unlike cash + ier said quickly.
normal.cn: 拼写上只保留一个 s，读音却像两个 s 连在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a tired worker counting notes behind a glass screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一位疲惫的职员在玻璃后面清点钞票。

abstract.en: Picture an officer handing over a sword and a badge.
abstract.cn: 想象一名军官交出佩剑和徽章。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer sliding open with coins stacked in neat rows.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉滑开，硬币排成整齐的几行。

examples.en: The cashier asked if I needed a bag.
examples.cn: 收银员问我要不要袋子。

examples.en: She worked as a cashier for two years.
examples.cn: 她当了两年收银员。

examples.en: The officer was cashiered after the inquiry.
examples.cn: 调查结束后那名军官被革职。

dict_mnemonic.text: cashier 可以拆成 cash 加 ier：整天守着 cash 的人，就是收银员。

root: 收银义源自法语 caissier（钱箱看管人），再往上可追到拉丁语 capsa（盒）；革职义另有来源，与意为打破、丢弃的动词相关。

sensesIntro.en: One line runs from the money box to the person who guards it, while a second line runs from breaking to dismissing an officer.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条线从钱箱走到看管钱箱的人，另一条线从打破走到把军官免职。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing beside the money box.
core.cn: 核心意象：守在钱箱旁边的人。

branches.en: The keeper of the box becomes the shop and bank worker.
branches.cn: 看管钱箱的人成了商店和银行的职员。

branches.en: The separate break-and-discard verb supplies the dismissal sense.
branches.cn: 另一个表示打破丢弃的动词提供了革职义。

branches.en: Everyday phrases such as bank cashier keep the job sense concrete.
branches.cn: bank cashier 这类日常搭配让职业义保持具体。

branches.en: Both strands involve handing something over: money at a counter or a commission in disgrace.
branches.cn: 两条线都涉及交出东西：柜台上交钱，或不光彩地交出职务。

branches.en: The officer sense stays formal and rare, mostly in military writing.
branches.cn: 军官义偏正式且少见，多出现在军事文字中。

intro.en: Cashier takes the -ier person ending and a few compounds; the rest of its family comes from the base cash.
intro.cn: cashier 带 -ier 表人词尾和少量复合词，其余词族成员来自词基 cash。

latinIntro.en: The money sense traces back through French to Latin capsa, a box.
latinIntro.cn: 钱款义经法语上溯到拉丁语 capsa（盒子）。

items.exampleCN: 革职终结了他的军旅生涯。

items.meaning: the counter where money is paid
items.example: Please go to the cashier's desk.
The cashbook was out of date.

latinEntries.example: Capsa lies behind cashier and cash.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capsa 是 cashier 与 cash 的源头。

definition_zh: 盒式磁带；暗盒；胶卷盒
definition_en: a small flat plastic case holding magnetic tape or film, used for recording sound or pictures
core_image: 一只扁平的小盒子，里面卷着长长的带子
scene: 她在阁楼里翻出一台旧录音机。The machine still played the cassette her father had recorded.
sceneCN: 这里 cassette 指「盒式磁带」（第 1 个义项：装着磁带的扁盒）；句意是这台机器还能播放她父亲录的那盘磁带。

senses.title: A case of magnetic tape
senses.definition: a small flat case containing magnetic tape that is played in a recorder
senses.definitionCN: 装着磁带、可放入录音机播放的扁平小盒
senses.example: He keeps his old cassettes in a shoebox.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旧磁带收在一个鞋盒里。
senses.why: The core image is a little box, and magnetic tape wound inside it is the use that made the word famous.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象就是一只小盒子，而卷在里面的磁带正是让这个词广为人知的用途。

senses.title: A lightproof film container
senses.definition: a lightproof case that holds photographic film and fits into a camera
senses.definitionCN: 装胶卷、可装入相机的防光小盒
senses.example: Load the cassette before you close the camera.
senses.exampleCN: 合上相机前先装好胶卷暗盒。
senses.why: This is the older photographic use: the same little case protects film from light instead of tape from dust.
senses.whyCN: 这是较早的摄影用法：同样的小盒子保护的是胶卷而不是磁带，防的是光而不是灰。

intro.en: Cassette is a French diminutive of a word for box, borrowed into English first for film and later for tape.
intro.cn: cassette 是法语中表示盒子的词的指小形式，英语先用它指胶卷盒，后指磁带盒。

items.en: Capsa meant a box, the same root that gives case and cash.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capsa 意为盒子，与 case、cash 同源。

items.en: Casse was a box, and cassette a little box, with the diminutive -ette.
items.cn: 法语 casse 指盒子，加指小词尾 -ette 后 cassette 就是小盒子。

items.en: English borrowed cassette for a small ornamental box.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 cassette，指小巧的装饰盒。

items.en: Photography applied the word to the lightproof case holding film.
items.cn: 十九世纪摄影术用该词指装胶卷的防光暗盒。

items.en: The tape recorder gave the word its most common modern meaning in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪磁带录音机赋予该词今天最常见的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the little-box root, while the meaning group gathers recording media.
note.cn: 形近组沿「小盒子」词根展开，近义组收录音载体。

entries.definition: a container for holding something
a very small tape cassette
a machine for playing tapes without a radio
entries.definitionCN: 不带收音功能的磁带播放机

entries.definition: a long thin strip coated for recording sound
entries.definitionCN: 涂有磁层用于录音的长带

entries.definition: a sealed case holding film or ink
entries.definitionCN: 装有胶卷或墨水的密封盒

entries.definition: a round holder that tape or film is wound on
entries.definitionCN: 缠绕磁带或胶卷的圆盘

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the little-box root, the -ette ending and the everyday player phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用小盒子词根、-ette 词尾以及日常播放机搭配。

normal.en: The ending -ette means little, as in cigarette and kitchenette, so a cassette is a little case.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ette 表示小，如 cigarette 和 kitchenette，所以 cassette 就是小盒子。

normal.en: Cassette and case share the Latin box root, which links the word to its shape.
normal.cn: cassette 与 case 共享拉丁语的盒子词根，这把词与外形连在一起。

normal.en: Cassette player and cassette recorder are the phrases that fix the tape sense.
normal.cn: cassette player 和 cassette recorder 是固定磁带义的搭配。

normal.en: Video cassette extends the same box to pictures as well as sound.
normal.cn: video cassette 把同一种盒子从声音扩展到画面。

normal.en: The plural cassettes simply adds an s, with no change of stress.
normal.cn: 复数 cassettes 只加一个 s，重音不变。

abstract.en: Picture a thin brown ribbon wound on two tiny wheels.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细细的棕色带子绕在两个小轮上。

abstract.en: Picture a finger pressing a stiff flap shut on a tape.
abstract.cn: 想象手指把磁带上硬硬的盖板按合。

abstract.en: Picture a dark room where film waits inside a sealed box.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里胶卷待在密封盒中等待曝光。

examples.en: The cassette jammed inside the player.
examples.cn: 磁带卡在播放机里了。

examples.en: She labelled every cassette with a date.
examples.cn: 她给每盘磁带都标了日期。

examples.en: This camera takes a small film cassette.
examples.cn: 这台相机使用小号胶卷暗盒。

dict_mnemonic.text: cassette 的词尾 -ette 表示小，可以记成「小 case」：一只装着磁带的小盒子。

root: 源自法语 cassette（小盒子），由 casse（盒子）加指小词尾 -ette 构成，更早可追到拉丁语 capsa（盒）。

sensesIntro.en: A little box first holds ornaments, then film, then magnetic tape, and each use keeps the same shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 一只小盒子先装装饰品，再装胶卷，再装磁带，每种用途都保留同一外形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small flat box with something wound inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只扁平小盒，里面卷着东西。

branches.en: Magnetic tape inside the box becomes the sound-recording sense.
branches.cn: 盒里的磁带成了录音义。

branches.en: Film inside the box becomes the photographic sense.
branches.cn: 盒里的胶卷成了摄影义。

branches.en: Both senses depend on the box keeping light and dust away from a sensitive strip.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖盒子替敏感的带子挡住光和灰尘。

branches.en: Player and recorder compounds keep this sense dominant today.
branches.cn: 播放机和录音机类复合词让这个义项在今天占据主导。

branches.en: The film sense now sounds old-fashioned but stays in camera manuals.
branches.cn: 胶卷义如今显得老旧，却仍留在相机说明书里。

intro.en: Cassette builds a thin family through compounds and the diminutive ending it already carries.
intro.cn: cassette 通过复合词和它本来就带的指小词尾形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The word descends from Latin capsa, a box, through the French diminutive cassette.
latinIntro.cn: 该词经法语指小形式 cassette 上溯到拉丁语 capsa（盒子）。

items.meaning: a small tape or film case
items.example: The cassette is in the drawer.

items.exampleCN: 盒子里装了四十盘磁带。
这台磁带播放机还能用。

items.meaning: a machine that records on tapes
items.example: He bought a cheap cassette recorder.
items.exampleCN: 他买了台便宜的盒式录音机。
这台口述机用的是微型磁带。

items.meaning: a tape player without a radio

items.example: The case has a strong hinge.
items.exampleCN: 这只盒子有结实的合页。

latinEntries.example: Capsa is the deep root of cassette.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capsa 是 cassette 的深层词根。

latinEntries.example: French cassette added the sense of small.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 法语 cassette 加上了「小」的含义。

definition_zh: 投掷；投射；选派角色；演员阵容；铸造
definition_en: to throw something, to send light or a look in a direction, to choose actors for roles, or to pour metal into a shape
core_image: 把手中的东西用力甩出去
scene: 导演在排练厅里念出名单。The director cast two young actors in the leading roles.
sceneCN: 这里 cast 指「选派角色」（第 2 个义项：为戏剧挑选演员）；句意是导演让两位年轻演员出演主角。

pos.zh: 投掷；投射；选派角色；铸造

senses.title: To throw something
senses.definition: to throw something with force, especially so that it lands some distance away
senses.definitionCN: 用力把某物扔出去，尤指扔到较远处
senses.example: He cast the rope toward the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 他把绳子抛向岸边。
senses.why: The Norse source simply meant to throw, and that physical act remains the core of every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语源词本义就是扔，这个身体动作始终是后面所有义项的核心。

senses.title: To choose actors for roles
senses.definition: to select actors for the parts in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 为戏剧或电影中的角色挑选演员
senses.example: They cast her as the queen.
senses.exampleCN: 他们让她演女王。
senses.why: Choosing an actor is pictured as throwing a person into a role, as if into a mould.
senses.whyCN: 选演员被想象成把人投进一个角色里，就像投进模具。

senses.title: The group of actors
senses.definition: all the actors who perform in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 参与一部戏剧或电影演出的全体演员
senses.example: The whole cast came on stage for the applause.
senses.exampleCN: 全体演员上台接受掌声。
senses.why: Once people have been thrown into their parts, the collection of them takes the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 人一旦被投进各自的角色，这一群人就沿用了同一个名词。

senses.title: To send light or a look
senses.definition: to cause light, shadow or a glance to fall on something
senses.definitionCN: 使光、影或目光落到某物上
senses.example: The tall buildings cast long shadows.
senses.exampleCN: 高楼投下长长的影子。
senses.why: Light thrown from a source behaves like an object thrown forward, so the verb covers casting shadows.
senses.whyCN: 从光源甩出的光就像被抛出的物体，于是动词也覆盖了投下影子。

senses.title: To pour metal into a mould
senses.definition: to pour melted metal into a shaped container so that it hardens into an object
senses.definitionCN: 把熔化的金属倒入模具，冷却后成为物件
senses.example: The workers cast the bell in one piece.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们一次浇铸成了这口钟。
senses.why: Molten metal is literally thrown into a mould, keeping the old sense of a forceful pour.
senses.whyCN: 熔化的金属确实是被「倒抛」进模具，保留了用力倾倒的旧义。

intro.en: Cast came from Old Norse rather than Latin, and one physical sense of throwing spread into acting, light and metalwork.
intro.cn: cast 来自古诺斯语而非拉丁语，一个扔的动作向外扩展到表演、光线和金属加工。

items.en: A reconstructed verb for throwing or tossing underlies the Norse word.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个表示投掷的原始日耳曼语动词，是诺斯语词的来源。

items.en: Kasta meant to throw, and Norse settlers brought it into northern English.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 kasta 意为投掷，随北欧移民进入英格兰北部。

items.en: Casten spreads from throwing objects to throwing light, looks and dice.
items.cn: 中古英语 casten 从扔物体扩展到投光、投目光和掷骰子。

items.en: Metalwork gives the sense of pouring molten metal into a mould.
items.cn: 金属加工带来把熔融金属倒入模具的义项。

items.en: The theatre takes cast for the selection of actors and then for the whole company.
items.cn: 十七世纪戏剧界用 cast 指挑选演员，进而指整个演员班底。

items.en: Modern English keeps all these branches, from casting a vote to a plaster cast.
items.cn: 现代英语保留全部分支，从投票到石膏铸型。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the casting and throwing family, while the meaning group lists other throwing verbs.
note.cn: 形近组沿铸造与投掷词族展开，近义组列出其他表示扔的动词。

entries.definition: the act of shaping metal or choosing actors
a person who casts metal, or a small wheel
a person left alone after a shipwreck
entries.definitionCN: 海难后被弃在荒处的人

entries.definition: to send something through the air with the hand
to throw something with great force
to throw something quickly and carelessly

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the single image of throwing and show how each phrase extends it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子守住「扔」这一个画面，并展示每个搭配如何延伸它。

normal.en: Every sense begins with a hand throwing: a rope, a vote, a shadow, a role or molten metal.
normal.cn: 每个义项都从一只手扔出去开始：绳子、选票、影子、角色或熔融金属。

normal.en: Cast a vote pictures the ballot as a small object thrown into a box.
normal.cn: cast a vote 把选票想象成被扔进箱子的小物件。

normal.en: Cast a shadow keeps the image literal: light throws a dark shape onto the ground.
normal.cn: cast a shadow 保留字面画面：光把一块暗形扔到地面上。

normal.en: The past tense is cast, not casted, so the verb looks unchanged.
normal.cn: 过去式是 cast 而不是 casted，所以动词看起来没有变化。

normal.en: Casting covers both metal and actors because both involve pouring something into a prepared shape.
normal.cn: casting 同时指铸金属和选演员，因为两者都是把东西倒进预备好的形状里。

abstract.en: Picture a fisherman flinging a net in a wide arc.
abstract.cn: 想象渔夫把网甩出一个大弧。

abstract.en: Picture a director pointing at one actor in a crowded room.
abstract.cn: 想象导演在挤满人的房间里指向一位演员。

abstract.en: Picture sparks flying as hot metal fills a clay mould.
abstract.cn: 想象炽热的金属注入泥模时火星四溅。

examples.en: She cast the line far into the river.
examples.cn: 她把钓线远远抛进河里。

examples.en: The film has a strong cast.
examples.cn: 这部电影的演员阵容很强。

examples.en: The tree cast a cool shadow over the bench.
examples.cn: 那棵树在长椅上投下一片凉影。

dict_mnemonic.text: cast 的核心动作就是「扔」：把绳子扔出去，把票扔进箱，把演员扔进角色，把铁水扔进模具。

root: 源自古诺斯语 kasta（投掷），属日耳曼语词，无拉丁语祖先；由「扔」这一动作扩展出投射、选角与铸造诸义。

sensesIntro.en: One throwing gesture gives the rope, the vote, the shadow, the actor and the molten metal.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个投掷动作先后给出绳子、选票、影子、演员和熔融金属。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand sending something forward through the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西向前甩到空中。

branches.en: The literal throw stays in fishing, dice and ropes.
branches.cn: 字面的扔保留在钓鱼、掷骰和抛绳中。

branches.en: Light thrown from a source lays a shadow down.
branches.cn: 从光源甩出的光把影子放倒在地上。

branches.en: Actors are thrown into parts, and the group of them becomes the cast.
branches.cn: 演员被投进角色，这一群人就成为演员阵容。

branches.en: Molten metal is poured into a mould and hardens into a cast object.
branches.cn: 熔融金属被倒入模具，凝固成铸件。

branches.en: Both keep the force of a deliberate, aimed pour or toss.
branches.cn: 两者都保留了有目标、有力度的倾倒或抛掷感。

intro.en: Cast builds compounds and agent nouns rather than taking classical affixes.
intro.cn: cast 主要构成复合词和表施动者的名词，不常接古典词缀。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor, so no Latin cognates are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: They cast the net at dawn.

items.meaning: the act of shaping or selecting
a metal worker or a small wheel
items.example: The caster lifted the hot mould.
items.exampleCN: 铸工抬起了滚烫的模具。

items.meaning: a statement about what will happen
a hard iron made by casting
items.example: The pan is made of cast iron.

definition_zh: 城堡；堡垒；车（国际象棋）
definition_en: a large strong building with thick walls and towers, built to defend a place, or the rook in chess
core_image: 建在高处的石墙与塔楼
scene: 旅行团沿着山路走到一座石砌建筑前。The guide explained how the castle had survived three sieges.
sceneCN: 这里 castle 指「城堡」（第 1 个义项：带厚墙与塔楼的防御建筑）；句意是导游讲解这座城堡如何熬过三次围攻。

senses.title: A fortified stone building
senses.definition: a large building with thick walls, towers and often a moat, built to resist attack
senses.definitionCN: 带厚墙、塔楼，常有护城河，为抵御进攻而建的大型建筑
senses.example: The castle stands on a hill above the town.
senses.exampleCN: 城堡坐落在小镇上方的山丘上。
senses.why: The Latin source was a small fort, and the stone walls and towers grew out of that defensive core.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源词指小要塞，石墙与塔楼正是从这一防御核心长出来的。

senses.title: The rook in chess
senses.definition: one of the two pieces in chess shaped like a tower, moving in straight lines
senses.definitionCN: 国际象棋中形似塔楼、沿直线行走的两个棋子之一
senses.example: He moved his castle to the open file.
senses.exampleCN: 他把车移到开放线上。
senses.why: The chess piece was carved as a turret, so the tower shape lent its name to the piece.
senses.whyCN: 这枚棋子被雕成小塔楼，于是塔楼的名称就借给了它。

intro.en: Castle descends from a Latin diminutive of a word for fort, and the chess piece borrowed its tower shape.
intro.cn: castle 源自拉丁语中表示要塞的词的指小形式，棋子则借用了它的塔楼外形。

items.en: Castrum meant a fortified camp, and its plural castra named a fort.
items.cn: 拉丁语 castrum 指设防营地，复数 castra 指要塞。

items.en: Castellum, a little fort, is the diminutive that leads to the English word.
items.cn: 指小形式 castellum 意为小要塞，是通向英语词的直接来源。

items.en: Castel enters Old English through Latin and Anglo-Norman French.
items.cn: castel 经拉丁语和盎格鲁诺曼法语进入古英语。

items.en: Castle settles as the word for a nobleman's fortified stone home.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，castle 固定指贵族设防的石砌宅邸。

items.en: The word also names the tower-shaped rook and the sandcastle on the beach.
items.cn: 现代英语中，它也指塔楼形的国际象棋车和沙滩上的沙堡。

note.en: The look-alike group stays with the Latin fort root, and the meaning group gathers other strongholds.
note.cn: 形近组留在拉丁语要塞词根内，近义组收其他坚固据点。

entries.definition: the governor of a castle
built with battlements like a castle
a large French country house or castle
a large strong building used for defence
entries.definitionCN: 用于防御的大型坚固建筑

entries.definition: the large official home of a ruler
a tall narrow building or part of one
entries.definitionCN: 高而窄的建筑物或其一部分

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin fort root, the chess shape and the sandcastle image.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用拉丁语要塞词根、棋子的形状和沙堡的画面。

normal.en: The Latin root castrum, a fort, also hides in castellum, the little fort behind castle.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词根 castrum（要塞）也藏在 castellum 里，后者正是 castle 背后的「小要塞」。

normal.en: The chess castle is simply a tower carved in wood or plastic.
normal.cn: 国际象棋里的车不过是一座用木头或塑料雕成的塔楼。

normal.en: Sand castle keeps the word alive on every beach, with walls and towers in miniature.
normal.cn: sand castle 让这个词活在每片沙滩上，用缩小版的墙和塔。

normal.en: Castle in the air means a plan with no foundation, like a castle built on nothing.
normal.cn: castle in the air 指没有根基的计划，就像建在虚空里的城堡。

normal.en: Only the plural castles is needed, since the noun has no verb use here.
normal.cn: 这里只需复数 castles，因为该名词在此没有动词用法。

abstract.en: Picture a grey wall rising above a moat at sunset.
abstract.cn: 想象日落时一道灰墙从护城河上方升起。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden tower sliding across a chessboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一座木塔在棋盘上滑动。

abstract.en: Picture a child patting wet sand into a tiny turret.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子把湿沙拍成一座小塔。

examples.en: The old castle is open to visitors in summer.
examples.cn: 这座古堡夏天对游客开放。

examples.en: They built a sand castle near the water.
examples.cn: 他们在水边堆了一座沙堡。

examples.en: His plan was a castle in the air.
examples.cn: 他的计划只是空中楼阁。

dict_mnemonic.text: castle 可以想成「卡住」的石头：一层层石头卡在一起，垒成高墙和塔楼。

root: 源自拉丁语 castellum（小要塞），是 castrum（设防营地）的指小形式，经古英语 castel 进入现代拼写。

sensesIntro.en: A small Latin fort grows into a stone home with towers, and its tower shape then names the chess piece.
sensesIntro.cn: 拉丁语的小要塞长成带塔楼的石砌宅邸，塔楼外形又给国际象棋的棋子命了名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick stone walls and towers on high ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：高地上的厚石墙与塔楼。

branches.en: Defence stays the first job of the building through the Middle Ages.
branches.cn: 在整个中世纪，防御始终是这座建筑的首要功能。

branches.en: The tower silhouette is copied onto the chessboard.
branches.cn: 塔楼的轮廓被复制到了棋盘上。

branches.en: Later castles become grand homes as much as forts.
branches.cn: 后来的城堡既是堡垒，也成为气派的宅邸。

branches.en: Both senses keep the tower as their shared outline.
branches.cn: 两个义项都以塔楼作为共同轮廓。

branches.en: The sandcastle is a playful miniature of the same walls.
branches.cn: 沙堡就是同样城墙的玩闹缩微版。

intro.en: Castle forms a small family through the -an and -ated endings and a few compounds.
intro.cn: castle 通过 -an、-ated 词尾和少量复合词形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base castrum, a fort, also appears in place names such as Chester and Lancaster.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 castrum（要塞）也出现在 Chester、Lancaster 等地名中。

items.example: The valley is full of castles.
items.exampleCN: 这条山谷里到处是城堡。

items.example: The castellan met them at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 城堡主在大门迎接他们。

items.example: The house has a castellated roof.
items.exampleCN: 这所房子有城堡式的屋顶。

items.example: The tide washed the sandcastle away.
They stayed in a chateau in the Loire.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在卢瓦尔河畔的一座庄园里。

items.example: Castrum survives in many place names.
items.exampleCN: castrum 存留在许多地名中。

items.example: Castellum is the direct source of castle.
items.exampleCN: castellum 是 castle 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Castrum named Roman marching camps.
latinEntries.exampleCN: castrum 指罗马军队的营寨。

definition_zh: 随意的；非正式的；漫不经心的；临时的
definition_en: relaxed and informal in manner or dress, not showing much care, or happening by chance and without a plan
core_image: 没有事先安排、随手就来的样子
scene: 公司周五允许员工不穿西装。On Fridays the office has a casual dress code.
sceneCN: 这里 casual 指「随意的」（第 1 个义项：不正式、轻松的穿着方式）；句意是每逢周五，办公室执行休闲着装规定。

pos.zh: 随意的；非正式的；漫不经心的；临时的

senses.title: Relaxed and informal
senses.definition: relaxed in style, not formal or planned, especially of clothes or gatherings
senses.definitionCN: 风格轻松，不正式或没有安排，尤指衣着或聚会
senses.example: He wore casual clothes to the dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着休闲服去参加晚宴。
senses.why: What happens by chance has no ceremony, so dress without ceremony becomes casual dress.
senses.whyCN: 偶然发生的事没有仪式感，于是不带仪式感的穿着就成了 casual 的穿着。

senses.title: Showing little care
senses.definition: done without attention or serious thought, sometimes causing harm
senses.definitionCN: 做事不加注意或不认真思考，有时造成损害
senses.example: A casual remark hurt her feelings.
senses.exampleCN: 一句随口的话伤了她的心。
senses.why: An unplanned act is also an unconsidered one, so the chance sense shades into carelessness.
senses.whyCN: 没有计划的行为也往往没有经过思考，于是偶然义渐渐带上马虎义。

senses.title: Temporary or occasional
senses.definition: employed for a short time or happening at irregular intervals
senses.definitionCN: 短期受雇的，或间隔不固定地发生的
senses.example: The hotel hires casual staff in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店夏天雇临时工。
senses.why: Work that comes by chance rather than by contract is casual work, done by casual workers.
senses.whyCN: 靠机会而非合同来的工作就是临时工作，由临时工来做。

intro.en: Casual goes back to the Latin word for a fall or event, so its first meaning is simply what happens by chance.
intro.cn: casual 可追到拉丁语中表示落下或事件的词，所以它最初的意思就是偶然发生的。

items.en: Casus meant a fall or an event, from cadere, to fall.
items.cn: 拉丁语 casus 意为落下或事件，源自动词 cadere（落下）。

items.en: Casualis described whatever happened by chance rather than by design.
items.cn: casualis 形容偶然发生、并非有意安排的事。

items.en: Casuel carried the chance sense into medieval French and then into English.
items.cn: 古法语 casuel 把偶然义带入中古法语，再进入英语。

items.en: English casual first means happening by chance, without plan or regularity.
items.cn: 英语 casual 最初指偶然发生、没有计划或规律。

items.en: The word extends to informal dress, relaxed manners and short-term work.
items.cn: 此后词义扩展到休闲衣着、随便的举止和短期工作。

items.en: Casual Friday and casual wear now fix the relaxed sense in everyday use.
items.cn: casual Friday 与 casual wear 让轻松义在日常用语中固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the chance root through its adverbs and nouns, while the meaning group offers nearby adjectives.
note.cn: 形近组沿偶然这一词根经副词与名词展开，近义组给出相近的形容词。

entries.definition: in a relaxed or careless way
the quality of being informal
a person killed or injured in an accident or war
entries.definitionCN: 在事故或战争中死伤的人

entries.definition: relaxed and without strict rules
calm and not worried
happening by chance, not on purpose

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie casual to the event root, to the -ly adverb and to the everyday dress phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 casual 与事件词根、-ly 副词和日常着装搭配连起来。

normal.en: Casual shares its root with case: both come from casus, an event that falls out.
normal.cn: casual 与 case 同根，都来自 casus，即落下来的事件。

normal.en: Casualty began as a chance event and now means a person hurt by one.
normal.cn: casualty 最初指偶然事件，现在指在事件中受伤的人。

normal.en: Casual clothes and casual Friday keep the informal sense visible every week.
normal.cn: casual clothes 和 casual Friday 每周都在提醒非正式这一含义。

normal.en: The -ly adverb casually simply adds the manner sense to the adjective.
normal.cn: 副词 casually 只是在形容词上加了方式义。

normal.en: More casual and most casual take a helper word because the adjective is long.
normal.cn: 因为词形较长，比较级和最高级用 more 与 most 来构成。

abstract.en: Picture a man in sandals at a formal dinner, completely at ease.
abstract.cn: 想象一位穿凉鞋出席正式晚宴却毫不拘束的男子。

abstract.en: Picture a remark tossed out without thinking, then landing hard.
abstract.cn: 想象一句没经思考就抛出的话，落地却很重。

abstract.en: Picture a worker hired for one busy weekend and paid by the day.
abstract.cn: 想象一个只在忙碌周末受雇、按天结钱的工人。

examples.en: The party was casual, so nobody dressed up.
examples.cn: 聚会很随意，所以没人特意打扮。

examples.en: He made a casual remark about the weather.
examples.cn: 他随口说了句天气的话。

examples.en: The factory takes on casual workers at harvest time.
examples.cn: 工厂在收获季节雇临时工。

dict_mnemonic.text: casual 里有 case：把生活看成一件件偶然落下的 case，穿着随意、说话随口都叫 casual。

root: 源自拉丁语 casualis（偶然的），再由 casus（落下、事件）派生，与 case 同根。

sensesIntro.en: What happens by chance needs no ceremony, no care and no long contract, so one root yields informality, carelessness and temporary work.
sensesIntro.cn: 偶然发生的事既不需要仪式，也不需要用心和长期合同，于是一个词根给出随意、马虎和临时这三层意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something that simply falls out without plan.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有计划、自己落下来的事。

branches.en: Chance work is work without a long agreement.
branches.cn: 偶然来的工作就是没有长期约定的工作。

branches.en: An occasion without ceremony lets clothes become casual.
branches.cn: 不带仪式的场合格调，让穿着也变得休闲。

branches.en: A remark made without thought is the careless side of the same root.
branches.cn: 未经思考的话就是同一词根的马虎一面。

branches.en: Both senses lack preparation, one in style and one in attention.
branches.cn: 两个义项都缺准备，一个缺在风格，一个缺在注意力。

branches.en: Relaxed dress and short-term work both sit outside formal rules.
branches.cn: 休闲着装与短期工作都处在正式规则之外。

intro.en: Casual takes the -ly and -ness endings and one old noun, casualty, that drifted far from its root.
intro.cn: casual 接 -ly 与 -ness 词尾，另有一个离开词根很远的旧名词 casualty。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin casualis, from casus, the same event word behind case and occasion.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 casualis，出自 casus，与 case、occasion 共享同一个事件词。

items.example: The casualness of the office surprised him.
items.exampleCN: 办公室的随意气氛让他吃惊。

items.meaning: a day when informal dress is allowed
items.meaningCN: 允许穿休闲装的工作日
items.exampleCN: 休闲星期五是上个月开始的。

items.example: Casualis is the Latin source of casual.
items.exampleCN: casualis 是 casual 的拉丁语来源。
casus 也是英语 case 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Casualis described unplanned events.
latinEntries.exampleCN: casualis 形容没有计划的事件。

latinEntries.example: Casus lies behind case and casual.
latinEntries.exampleCN: casus 是 case 与 casual 的源头。

definition_zh: 猫；猫科动物
definition_en: a small furry animal with whiskers and soft paws, often kept as a pet, or any animal of the same family
core_image: 柔软无声的脚掌和一双竖起的耳朵
scene: 深夜院子里传来轻轻的脚步。A grey cat slipped through the fence and disappeared.
sceneCN: 这里 cat 指「猫」（第 1 个义项：常见的小型家养动物）；句意是一只灰猫从篱笆缝里钻过去不见了。

collocations.phrase: let the cat out of the bag

senses.title: A small domestic feline
senses.definition: a small furry animal with soft paws and whiskers, kept as a pet or kept to catch mice
senses.definitionCN: 一种毛茸茸、脚掌柔软、有胡须的小动物，常被当作宠物或用来捕鼠
senses.example: The cat slept on the warm windowsill.
senses.exampleCN: 猫在温暖的窗台上睡着了。
senses.why: The core image of soft paws and pointed ears belongs to the everyday house cat.
senses.whyCN: 柔软脚掌与尖耳朵这一核心意象，正属于日常所见家猫。

senses.title: Any member of the feline family
senses.definition: any wild or domestic animal of the family that includes lions, tigers and cats
senses.definitionCN: 包括狮、虎和家猫在内的猫科中的任何野生或家养动物
senses.example: The lion is a big cat with a loud roar.
senses.exampleCN: 狮子是一种会大声吼叫的大型猫科动物。
senses.why: Biologists group the house cat with its large wild relatives, so cat widens to the whole family.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家把家猫与其大型野生近亲归为一类，于是 cat 扩展为整个猫科。

intro.en: Cat is an old English word whose deeper origin is uncertain, though it is usually traced through Late Latin cattus.
intro.cn: cat 是古英语旧词，更深来源不确定，通常认为经由晚期拉丁语 cattus 传来。

items.en: Cattus is the first well-recorded form, probably borrowed from an African or Semitic language.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 cattus 是较早的可靠记录形式，可能借自非洲或闪米特语。

items.en: Catt appears in Old English for the domestic animal, with separate words for male and female.
items.cn: 古英语 catt 指家猫，公猫与母猫另有说法。

items.en: Cat replaces the older plural forms and becomes the general word.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，cat 取代旧的复数形式，成为通称。

items.en: The word enters idioms such as let the cat out of the bag.
items.cn: 该词进入「let the cat out of the bag」等习语。

items.en: Cat extends to big cats and to compounds such as cat food and tomcat.
items.cn: 现代英语中 cat 扩展到大型猫科，并构成 cat food、tomcat 等复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group follows English formations on cat, and the meaning group lists felines and their young.
note.cn: 形近组沿英语中由 cat 构成的词展开，近义组列出猫科动物及幼崽。

entries.definition: saying unkind things about others
moving or looking like a cat
the quality of being spiteful
a young cat
relating to cats, or a cat-like animal
entries.definitionCN: 与猫有关的，或猫一样的动物

entries.definition: a male cat

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin source, the idioms and the small family of cat compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用拉丁语来源、常见习语以及 cat 的小词族。

normal.en: Cat, kitten and tomcat split the animal by age and sex, all inside one short family.
normal.cn: cat、kitten、tomcat 按年龄和性别划分这种动物，都在一个短短的词族里。

normal.en: Let the cat out of the bag pictures a secret escaping like an animal from a sack.
normal.cn: 「let the cat out of the bag」把秘密想象成从袋子里跑出来的动物。

normal.en: Rain cats and dogs is pure idiom, with no link to the animal's habits.
normal.cn: rain cats and dogs 纯属习语，与猫狗的真实习性无关。

normal.en: Big cat covers lions and tigers, showing how one word widens to a whole family.
normal.cn: big cat 覆盖狮子和老虎，说明一个词如何扩展到整个科。

normal.en: The plural cats is regular, so the noun needs only one extra letter.
normal.cn: 复数 cats 变化规则，名词只多一个字母。

abstract.en: Picture a cat landing without a sound on a narrow wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只猫无声地落在窄墙上。

abstract.en: Picture green eyes opening in a dark garden.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中一双绿眼睛睁开。

abstract.en: Picture a kitten tangled in a ball of wool.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小猫缠在毛线球里。

examples.en: The cat followed me all the way home.
examples.cn: 那只猫一路跟着我回家。

examples.en: She feeds every stray cat in the street.
examples.cn: 她喂街上每一只流浪猫。

examples.en: A tiger is a big cat.
examples.cn: 老虎是一种大型猫科动物。

dict_mnemonic.text: cat 只有三个字母，读音短促像猫叫：记住这个短音，就记住了这种轻声走路的动物。

root: 古英语 catt，通常认为经晚期拉丁语 cattus 传来，更深来源不确定，可能与非洲或闪米特语有关。

sensesIntro.en: The small domestic animal gives the everyday sense, and biology widens the same name to lions and tigers.
sensesIntro.cn: 家养的小动物给出日常义，生物学又把同一个名称扩展到狮虎。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft paws, whiskers and pointed ears.
core.cn: 核心意象：柔软的脚掌、胡须与尖耳朵。

branches.en: The house pet keeps the soft paws and the quiet walk.
branches.cn: 家猫保留了软脚掌和无声的步伐。

branches.en: Biology extends the name to lions, tigers and leopards.
branches.cn: 生物学把这个名称扩展到狮、虎和豹。

branches.en: Farm cats earn their place by catching mice.
branches.cn: 农场的猫靠捕鼠赢得自己的位置。

branches.en: Both share the same body plan, only the size differs.
branches.cn: 两者身体结构相同，只是大小不同。

branches.en: Idioms turn the cat into a figure of secrets and heavy rain.
branches.cn: 习语把猫变成秘密与大雨的形象。

intro.en: Cat forms a small family with -y, -like and -ness, plus a few familiar compounds.
intro.cn: cat 通过 -y、-like、-ness 以及几个常见复合词形成小词族。

latinIntro.en: The recorded Latin form is cattus, itself probably borrowed from outside the Latin family.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的拉丁语形式是 cattus，它本身很可能借自拉丁语族之外。

items.example: Two cats sat on the wall.
Her catty remark spoiled the evening.
items.exampleCN: 她那句刻薄话毁了整个晚上。

items.example: There was real cattiness in the office.
items.exampleCN: 办公室里确有刻薄之风。

items.example: Cattus is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: cattus 是较早的记录形式。

latinEntries.example: Cattus spread across medieval Europe.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cattus 传遍了中世纪的欧洲。

definition_zh: 目录；商品目录；一连串；编入目录
definition_en: a complete list of items arranged in order, especially goods for sale or books in a library, or to make such a list
core_image: 把东西一件件点清、按顺序列成单子
scene: 图书馆员在书架间查找一本书。She opened the online catalog and typed the title.
sceneCN: 这里 catalog 指「目录」（第 1 个义项：图书按顺序编排的清单）；句意是她打开联机目录，输入书名。

senses.title: An ordered list of items
senses.definition: a list of names, goods or books put in a fixed order for reference
senses.definitionCN: 把名称、商品或书籍按固定顺序排列、供查检的清单
senses.example: The store mails a catalog before Christmas.
senses.exampleCN: 商店在圣诞节前寄出商品目录。
senses.why: The Greek source meant a counting-off, so the list is first of all things named one by one.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源词意为逐一点数，所以目录首先是被一件件念出来的东西。

senses.title: A series of unwanted things
senses.definition: a long series of events or faults, usually unpleasant ones
senses.definitionCN: 一长串事件或过失，通常指令人不快的
senses.example: The report is a catalog of failures.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是一连串的失败记录。
senses.why: A list counts items in order, and when the items are faults the same word means a whole series of them.
senses.whyCN: 清单按顺序清点条目，当条目是过失时，同一个词就表示一整串过失。

senses.title: To list items in order
senses.definition: to arrange names or objects into an ordered list for later use
senses.definitionCN: 把名称或物品排成有序清单，以便日后查用
senses.example: They cataloged every letter in the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把档案中的每封信都编了目。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: instead of reading the list, you make it.
senses.whyCN: 动词义是名词义的反向操作：不是读清单，而是把清单做出来。

intro.en: Catalog comes from a Greek verb meaning to count off, and it reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: catalog 来自一个意为逐一点数的希腊语动词，经拉丁语和法语进入英语。

items.en: Kata meant down or according to, and legein meant to say or count.
items.cn: 希腊语 kata 表示向下或按照，legein 表示说或点数。

items.en: Katalogos was a list or register, literally a counting off of items.
items.cn: katalogos 意为清单或名录，字面就是逐项点数。

items.en: Catalogus carried the Greek list word into the scholarly language of Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语 catalogus 把这个希腊语清单词带入欧洲学术语言。

items.en: French catalogue spread the word through book trade and library practice.
items.cn: 法语 catalogue 通过图书贸易与图书馆实务推广该词。

items.en: English catalog first names a list of books or goods in a fixed order.
items.cn: 英语 catalog 最初指按固定顺序排列的书目或货单。

items.en: The word spreads to mail-order selling, computing and figurative lists of faults.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词扩展到邮购、计算机以及比喻性的过失清单。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the Greek list word and its English endings, while the meaning group gathers other kinds of ordered records.
note.cn: 形近组保留希腊语清单词及英语词尾，近义组收其他有序记录。

entries.definition: the British spelling of the same word
a person who makes a catalog
the work of listing items
a set of items written one below another
an alphabetical guide to pages in a book
entries.definitionCN: 按字母排列、指向书中页码的索引

entries.definition: a full count of goods in stock
entries.definitionCN: 对库存货物的全面清点

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek counting root, the library phrases and the American spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用希腊语点数词根、图书馆搭配以及美式拼写。

normal.en: Catalog and catalogue differ only by the ue ending, so remember one and you have both.
normal.cn: catalog 与 catalogue 只差结尾的 ue，记住一个就记住了两个。

normal.en: The Greek root legein, to say, hides in catalog just as it does in logic and dialogue.
normal.cn: 希腊语词根 legein（说）藏在 catalog 里，也藏在 logic 与 dialogue 里。

normal.en: Library catalog and product catalog put the word where it is most often seen.
normal.cn: library catalog 与 product catalog 把词放在最常见的两种场合。

normal.en: A catalog of errors turns a neutral list into a long complaint.
normal.cn: a catalog of errors 把中性的清单变成了一长串抱怨。

normal.en: American spelling drops the ue and doubles nothing in cataloging, keeping one l.
normal.cn: 美式拼写去掉 ue，cataloging 也只保留一个 l。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk reciting names one by one and ticking each off.
abstract.cn: 想象一位职员一件件念出名称，再逐一打勾。

abstract.en: Picture a fat paper catalog lying open at the toy section.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚厚的纸质目录摊开在玩具那一页。

abstract.en: Picture shelves of small drawers, each with a neat label.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排小抽屉，每格都贴着整齐的标签。

examples.en: The museum published a catalog of its paintings.
examples.cn: 博物馆出版了藏画目录。

examples.en: She ordered the shoes from a catalog.
examples.cn: 她从目录上订购了那双鞋。

examples.en: The librarian cataloged the new books in a week.
examples.cn: 图书管理员一周内给新书编好了目。

dict_mnemonic.text: catalog 可以拆成 cata 加 log：log 是记录，把东西一件件记下来，就成了目录。

root: 源自希腊语 katalogos（清单、名册），由 kata（按照）与 legein（说、点数）构成，经拉丁语 catalogus 与法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Counting items aloud gives the list, the list extends to goods and books, and the same word names a series of faults.
sensesIntro.cn: 把东西逐一点数得出清单，清单扩展到商品与图书，同一个词又指一连串过失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: items named one by one and set down in order.
core.cn: 核心意象：把东西一件件念出来，按顺序记下。

branches.en: A shop catalog keeps goods in a fixed order for buyers.
branches.cn: 商店目录把商品按固定顺序排给买家看。

branches.en: A library catalog does the same for books and readers.
branches.cn: 图书馆目录对图书和读者做同样的事。

branches.en: The verb is the act of building the list.
branches.cn: 动词义就是编制这份清单的动作。

branches.en: When the listed items are faults, the list becomes a complaint.
branches.cn: 当列出的条目是过失时，清单就变成了控诉。

branches.en: Noun and verb differ only in whether the list is read or made.
branches.cn: 名词与动词只差在清单是被读还是被做出来。

intro.en: Catalog builds its family with -er and -ing, plus the British spelling catalogue.
intro.cn: catalog 用 -er 与 -ing 构词，另有英式拼写 catalogue。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form catalogus preserves the Greek list word almost unchanged.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 catalogus 几乎原样保留了希腊语的清单词。

items.example: The catalog is on the desk.
He cataloged the stamps by year.

items.exampleCN: 编目员核对了每个书名。

items.meaning: the same word in British English

items.exampleCN: catalogus 进入了中世纪拉丁语。

latinEntries.example: Catalogus kept the Greek meaning intact.
latinEntries.exampleCN: catalogus 完整保留了希腊语含义。

definition_zh: 目录；目录册；一系列；编入目录
definition_en: a book or list that names things in order, especially goods or library holdings, or to enter items into such a list
core_image: 一页页排好的条目，像账簿一样整齐
scene: 拍卖行整理本季的拍品。The auction house printed a thick catalogue of paintings.
sceneCN: 这里 catalogue 指「目录册」（第 1 个义项：装订成册的条目清单）；句意是拍卖行印了一本厚厚的画作目录。

senses.title: A book listing items
senses.definition: a printed book or document that lists goods, works of art or books in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序列出商品、艺术品或书籍的印刷册子或文件
senses.example: The gallery sent me its new catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊给我寄来了新目录。
senses.why: The Greek list word was first spoken, then written, and finally bound as a book.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语的清单词先从口头念出，再写下来，最后装订成册。

senses.title: A long series of events
senses.definition: a continuous series of things, especially unpleasant ones, that seem to be counted off
senses.definitionCN: 连续发生的一串事情，尤指像是被逐项数出的不快之事
senses.example: The year was a catalogue of mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年是一连串错误的集合。
senses.why: If a catalogue counts items, then a year full of faults can itself be read as a catalogue.
senses.whyCN: 既然目录是逐项清点，那么满是过失的一年本身也能读成一份目录。

senses.title: To enter items in a list
senses.definition: to record objects or works in an ordered list, often with numbers and descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 把物品或作品记入有序清单，常附编号与说明
senses.example: They catalogued the letters before storing them.
senses.exampleCN: 他们先把信件编目，然后才归档。
senses.why: To catalogue is to do the counting work that produces a catalogue.
senses.whyCN: 编目就是做那份清点工作，从而产生一份目录。

intro.en: Catalogue keeps the French spelling of the Greek list word, and its -ue ending still marks the British form today.
intro.cn: catalogue 保留了希腊语清单词的法语拼写，结尾的 -ue 至今是英式拼写的标志。

items.en: Katalogos meant a list or register, from kata and legein, to say or count.
items.cn: 希腊语 katalogos 意为清单或名录，由 kata 与 legein（说、点数）构成。

items.en: Catalogus carried the word into the written culture of the Roman world.
items.cn: 拉丁语 catalogus 把该词带入罗马世界的书写文化。

items.en: Catalogue gave English the -ue spelling that British usage still prefers.
items.cn: 法语 catalogue 给英语留下了英式用法偏爱的 -ue 拼写。

items.en: Catalogue is recorded as a list of names or books arranged for reference.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语中，catalogue 已有按序排列名称或书籍的记录。

items.en: Art dealers and libraries make the printed catalogue a standard tool.
items.cn: 十九世纪艺术品商人与图书馆把印刷目录变成标准工具。

items.en: The phrase a catalogue of disasters fixes the figurative series sense.
items.cn: 短语 a catalogue of disasters 固定了比喻性的「一连串」义。

note.en: The look-alike group stays with the -ue spelling and its derivatives, and the meaning group gives other records.
note.cn: 形近组留在 -ue 拼写及其派生词内，近义组给出其他记录形式。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same word
a person who compiles a catalogue
the process of listing items
an official list kept as a record
a detailed list of goods in stock
a book listing names, addresses or services
entries.definitionCN: 列出名称、地址或服务的册子

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the French -ue ending, the auction phrases and the disaster idiom.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用法语式 -ue 词尾、拍卖场搭配以及灾难习语。

normal.en: The -ue ending is the British mark, just as in colour and theatre.
normal.cn: 结尾 -ue 是英式标志，就像 colour 与 theatre 的拼写。

normal.en: Catalogue and dialogue share the Greek root legein, to speak or count.
normal.cn: catalogue 与 dialogue 共享希腊语词根 legein（说或点数）。

normal.en: Auction catalogue and exhibition catalogue fix the printed-book sense.
normal.cn: auction catalogue 与 exhibition catalogue 固定了印刷册子义。

normal.en: A catalogue of disasters is a whole year of trouble read aloud.
normal.cn: a catalogue of disasters 就是把一整年的麻烦逐条念出来。

normal.en: Catalogue numbers give each listed work a small address of its own.
normal.cn: 目录编号给每件列出的作品一个小地址。

abstract.en: Picture a thick book with gilt numbers down the spine.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚书，书脊上印着烫金编号。

abstract.en: Picture an auctioneer tapping a page of listed paintings.
abstract.cn: 想象拍卖师敲着写满画作的那一页。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of boxes, each labelled with a neat number.
abstract.cn: 想象一整排箱子，每只都标着整齐的编号。

examples.en: The catalogue lists every piece in the show.
examples.cn: 目录列出了展览中的每件作品。

examples.en: She found the price in the auction catalogue.
examples.cn: 她在拍卖目录里找到了价格。

examples.en: The collection was catalogued over ten years.
examples.cn: 这批藏品用了十年时间编目。

dict_mnemonic.text: catalogue 里的 log 是记录：把展品一件件记进本子，就成了一本目录册。

root: 与 catalog 同源，出自希腊语 katalogos（清单），经拉丁语 catalogus 与法语 catalogue 进入英语，-ue 为法式拼写残留。

sensesIntro.en: A spoken counting-off becomes a printed book, then a year of misfortunes, while the verb names the counting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 口头的逐项点数变成印刷册子，再变成一年的不幸，而动词则指点数这个动作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered entries standing in neat rows.
core.cn: 核心意象：编了号、排成整齐行列的条目。

branches.en: The written list is bound and sold as a catalogue.
branches.cn: 写下的清单被装订起来，作为目录册出售。

branches.en: A run of bad events is counted off like entries.
branches.cn: 一连串坏事像条目一样被逐项数出。

branches.en: The verb performs the counting that fills the book.
branches.cn: 动词义执行填入册子的清点工作。

branches.en: Book and action are two sides of the same ordered record.
branches.cn: 册子与动作是同一份有序记录的两面。

branches.en: Both senses rely on the feeling of a long, orderly series.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖「长而有序的一串」这种感觉。

intro.en: Catalogue forms -er and -ing nouns and keeps the French -ue in every British spelling.
intro.cn: catalogue 构成 -er 与 -ing 名词，英式拼写始终保留法语式 -ue。

latinIntro.en: Latin catalogus kept the Greek list word, which French later reshaped as catalogue.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 catalogus 保留了希腊语清单词，法语后来把它改写成 catalogue。

items.example: The cataloguer noted a missing page.
items.exampleCN: 编目员注意到缺了一页。

items.meaning: the same word in American English

items.exampleCN: catalogus 见于中世纪图书馆。

latinEntries.example: Catalogus is the Latin bridge to English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: catalogus 是通向英语的拉丁语桥梁。

definition_zh: 抓住；接住；赶上；染上；听懂
definition_en: to take hold of something moving, to reach a bus or train in time, to get an illness, or to hear and understand something
core_image: 伸手一扑，把正在动的东西按在手里
scene: 球场上队友把球高高抛起。He jumped and caught the ball with one hand.
sceneCN: 这里 catch 指「接住」（第 1 个义项：用手抓住运动中的东西）；句意是他跳起来，单手接住了球。

pos.zh: 抓住；接住；赶上；染上；听懂

senses.title: To take hold of something moving
senses.definition: to stop and hold a moving object with the hands
senses.definitionCN: 用手拦住并握住运动中的物体
senses.example: She caught the keys he threw her.
senses.exampleCN: 她接住了他扔来的钥匙。
senses.why: The core image is a hand closing on something in flight, and that is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一只手合拢在飞行中的东西上，这也是最古老的义项。

senses.title: To reach a bus or train in time
senses.definition: to arrive early enough to get on a bus, train, plane or boat
senses.definitionCN: 到得够早，能登上公交、火车、飞机或船
senses.example: We ran and caught the last bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们跑着赶上了末班车。
senses.why: A departing vehicle is a moving target, so boarding it in time is catching it.
senses.whyCN: 开走的车就是一个移动目标，及时登上它也就是「抓住」它。

senses.title: To get an illness
senses.definition: to become infected with a disease or pick up an illness from others
senses.definitionCN: 被疾病感染，或从他人那里染上病
senses.example: He caught a cold after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行之后他感冒了。
senses.why: An illness is pictured as something passing by that the body seizes.
senses.whyCN: 疾病被想象成从身边经过、被身体抓住的东西。

senses.title: To hear and understand
senses.definition: to manage to hear words or understand a joke or meaning
senses.definitionCN: 设法听清话语，或理解笑话与含义
senses.example: I did not catch what she said.
senses.exampleCN: 我没听清她说什么。
senses.why: Understanding is pictured as grabbing hold of words before they fly away.
senses.whyCN: 理解被想象成在话语飞走之前把它抓住。

intro.en: Catch came through northern French from a Latin verb meaning to try to seize, and its spelling kept the French sound.
intro.cn: catch 经法国北部方言上溯到拉丁语中意为试图抓取的动词，拼写保留了法语读音。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, and captare meant to keep trying to seize.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capere 意为拿取，captare 意为反复试图抓取。

items.en: Cachier meant to chase or hunt, a northern French form of the Latin verb.
items.cn: 古北法语 cachier 意为追捕，是拉丁语动词的北部方言形式。

items.en: Cacchen appears in the thirteenth century for chasing and seizing.
items.cn: 中古英语 cacchen 在十三世纪已指追逐与抓取。

items.en: The word extends to catching a train, catching cold and catching meaning.
items.cn: 此后词义扩展到赶车、受凉和听懂意思。

items.en: Modern idioms add catch fire, catch sight of and catch up with.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上着火、瞥见和追上等习语。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the English family of catch, while the meaning group lists other verbs for seizing.
note.cn: 形近组沿 catch 的英语词族展开，近义组列出其他表示抓取的动词。

entries.definition: a person or thing that catches
able to spread from person to person
entries.definitionCN: 能在人与人之间传染的

entries.definition: easy to remember and repeat
to take hold of something suddenly and firmly
to take something quickly with the hand
to take a person or animal prisoner

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie catch to its Latin seize root, to the irregular past caught and to common idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 catch 与拉丁语抓取词根、不规则过去式 caught 以及常见习语连起来。

normal.en: Catch and capture share the Latin root cap, to take, which explains why both mean seizing.
normal.cn: catch 与 capture 共享拉丁语词根 cap（拿取），这解释了为什么两者都表示抓。

normal.en: The past tense is caught, rhyming with taught and bought, all old irregular forms.
normal.cn: 过去式是 caught，与 taught、bought 押韵，都是古老的不规则形式。

normal.en: Catch a cold pictures the illness as a passing object you grab.
normal.cn: catch a cold 把疾病想象成一个路过、被你抓住的东西。

normal.en: Catch a train keeps the same move: you reach the departing vehicle in time.
normal.cn: catch a train 保留同一动作：你及时够到了正在离开的车。

normal.en: Catchy music is music that catches in your head and will not leave.
normal.cn: catchy 的音乐就是抓住你脑子、赶不走的音乐。

abstract.en: Picture a hand snapping shut around a thrown ball.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手啪地合拢，扣住飞来的球。

abstract.en: Picture a runner sliding through closing train doors.
abstract.cn: 想象奔跑者从正在合拢的车门间挤进去。

abstract.en: Picture a word flying past and being snatched out of the air.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词从耳边飞过，被凌空抓下。

examples.en: Can you catch the ball with your left hand?
examples.cn: 你能用左手接住球吗？

examples.en: I need to catch the early train tomorrow.
examples.cn: 我明天得赶早班火车。

examples.en: She caught a cold during the trip.
examples.cn: 她在旅途中感冒了。

dict_mnemonic.text: catch 短促有力，像手掌「咔」一下合上：抓住球、抓住车、抓住病、抓住话里的意思。

root: 源自古北法语 cachier（追捕），上溯拉丁语 captare（反复试图抓取），是 capere（拿取）的反复形式。

sensesIntro.en: One snatching gesture extends to vehicles, illnesses and words, because all of them are things that pass and can be seized.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个抓取动作扩展到车、病和话，因为它们都是经过身边、可以被抓住的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing on something in motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢在运动中的东西上。

branches.en: The literal hand closes on a ball, a rope or a key.
branches.cn: 字面义是手合拢在球、绳或钥匙上。

branches.en: A departing vehicle is caught by arriving in time.
branches.cn: 开走的车靠及时赶到而被「抓住」。

branches.en: An illness is caught as it passes through the air.
branches.cn: 疾病像从空气里经过时被抓住。

branches.en: Meaning is caught when the words are held long enough to be understood.
branches.cn: 话语被握住足够久、听明白了，意思就被抓住。

branches.en: Both depend on speed and timing rather than strength.
branches.cn: 两者都取决于速度和时机，而非力量。

intro.en: Catch forms agent and adjective nouns with -er, -ing and -y, and keeps an irregular past.
intro.cn: catch 用 -er、-ing、-y 构成名词与形容词，并保留不规则过去式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base capere, to take, is the same root behind capture, captive and accept.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 capere（拿取）也是 capture、captive 与 accept 的词根。

items.example: She catches every cold going round.
items.exampleCN: 流行什么感冒她都染上。

items.example: They caught the thief at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 他们在大门口抓住了小偷。

items.meaning: spreading, or in the act of seizing
items.meaningCN: 有传染性的，或正在抓取

items.example: The catcher signalled for a fast ball.
The song has a catchy chorus.
Captare is the source of catch.
items.exampleCN: captare 是 catch 的来源。
capere 也是 capture 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Capere is the base of many English words.
latinEntries.exampleCN: capere 是许多英语词的词基。

latinEntries.example: Captare passed into northern French.
latinEntries.exampleCN: captare 传入了法国北部方言。

definition_zh: 类别；种类；范畴
definition_en: a group of people or things that share a particular quality, or a basic class in philosophy and logic
core_image: 把一大堆东西分进贴着标签的格子
scene: 评委把参赛作品分成几组。Each entry was placed in a different category.
sceneCN: 这里 category 指「类别」（第 1 个义项：按共同特点划分的一组）；句意是每件参赛作品都被归入不同的类别。

senses.title: A class of similar things
senses.definition: a group of people or things that share a common feature and are treated together
senses.definitionCN: 具有共同特点、被放在一起处理的一组人或物
senses.example: These films belong to the same category.
senses.exampleCN: 这些影片属于同一类别。
senses.why: The Greek word was a public statement about what something is, and naming a class is exactly that kind of statement.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源词是对某物是什么的公开断言，而给一个类别命名正是这种断言。

senses.title: A basic class in logic
senses.definition: one of the most general classes used to analyse reality, such as quantity, quality or relation
senses.definitionCN: 用于分析现实的最普遍类别，如数量、性质或关系
senses.example: Kant listed twelve categories of understanding.
senses.exampleCN: 康德列出了十二个知性范畴。
senses.why: Philosophy takes the everyday class word and raises it to the widest possible divisions of thought.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把日常的类别词提升为思维中最宽泛的划分。

intro.en: Category began as a Greek word for a public accusation, then became the logical term for what can be stated of a thing.
intro.cn: category 最初是希腊语中公开指控的说法，后来成为逻辑学中「关于某物能说什么」的术语。

items.en: Agora was the public assembly, and agoreuein meant to speak in public.
items.cn: 希腊语 agora 指公民大会，agoreuein 意为当众发言。

items.en: Kategoria meant an accusation, a statement made publicly against someone.
items.cn: kategoria 意为指控，即当众针对某人作出的陈述。

items.en: Aristotle used the word for the basic ways something can be predicated, such as quantity or relation.
